policies.title: Solomon Islands: EU ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The in-force EU–Solomon Islands agreement expressly waives visas for ordinary passports of its defined Member States, excluding Ireland and the United Kingdom.
conditions: Article 2 defines a Member State as an EU Member State other than Ireland and the United Kingdom; the passport list maps only that defined cohort.
Article 3 covers valid ordinary passports for short stays and excludes paid activity. Article 4 sets the maximum at 90 days in any 180-day period.
This treaty does not establish a route for other European nationalities, residence holders, special documents, or paid activity.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: PRC ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The gazetted China–Solomon Islands agreement exempts valid ordinary PRC passports from visas for short visitor stays.
conditions: Article I covers valid ordinary PRC passports, with a maximum 30 days per stay and 90 days in a 180-day period. The corresponding PRC Foreign Ministry notice states the agreement took effect on 28 December 2024.

Article II requires use of ports open to international travellers and compliance with local law. Work, study, settlement, journalism and other prior-approval activities remain outside this visitor policy.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: UAE ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The gazetted UAE–Solomon Islands MOU exempts valid ordinary UAE passports from entry-visa requirements.
conditions: Articles 1 and 2 expressly cover valid UAE ordinary passports, entry, exit and transit without an entry visa or charge, and stays up to 90 days.
Article 5 excludes work and study unless the traveller first obtains the required permission. Article 6 limits use to international passenger border points.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: concessional ordinary passports receive a visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current legal notice designates this non-waiver subset of its listed nationalities for concessional entry, and government guidance says it need not apply in advance and receives a visitor visa on arrival.
conditions: Legal Notice No. 128 names this cohort and repeals earlier concessional notices. The government guidance says it does not apply in advance and is granted a visitor visa on arrival. The policy deliberately omits its China and covered-EU entries because specific current waiver instruments control those codes.
Arrival requires a passport valid for at least six months and a confirmed return or onward ticket; immigration retains ordinary entry and admission discretion.

This is visa_on_arrival, not visa-free admission. The current Immigration tourist page calls arrival issuance discretionary and gives inconsistent general tourist durations, so no uniform stay, extension, entry count, fee or port is assigned.

A July 2026 Division delivery-policy PDF claims the Minister repealed the concessional arrangement, but contains no approval date, approving authority, operative repeal date or later Gazette citation. The current Invest Solomons guidance still expressly applies Legal Notice No. 128. Recheck this policy if a signed superseding instrument is published.

China and the covered EU ordinary passports are excluded because the respective gazetted or in-force agreement directly establishes visa-free treatment; UAE is separately supported by its gazetted agreement.
